lessons: Implementation reached review with green checks. Review accepted the serial slot, re-gate ordering, tree-hash refusal, both rungs and the git seams. Keep all of it; fix only the unwind gap in the rebase failure paths.

A non-conflict GitError can arrive after the rebase has started, e.g. an untracked file that would be overwritten mid-replay. Abort the in-progress rebase before returning CandidateRebaseFinding, so the candidate worktree ends on its branch head.

Do not add a new public Git method: the criteria allow only three git.py additions. Inside rebase_stop_at_conflict, on a non-conflict failure, try rebase_abort and ignore its GitError (as `rebase` already does), then re-raise the original error.

Wrap the conflict-resolution loop in _rebase in try/except BaseException: abort the rebase, then re-raise. This covers conflicted_paths raising after a failed rebase_continue, and a regenerate process.run timeout.

Add a test where the rebase starts, then fails with no conflicted paths: an untracked file on the candidate that a main commit would overwrite. Assert typed gate_failed, HEAD equals the branch head, no rebase-merge/rebase-apply dir, and the slot is released.
Update REBASE_FAILURE_ROAD: the queue now restores the worktree itself, so the paved road should only name correcting the rebase precondition and retrying admission.
reason: Review snag on one concrete, fixable unwind gap with an explicit paved road; the rest of the implementation was accepted and all checks passed.
